detail.abstract: LLM agents that read news and call short-horizon market direction are easy to build, and many people are building them. We test one such system prospectively, against a protocol written in advance. A four-stage multi-agent pipeline (factor mapping, parallel news research, signal synthesis, prediction) made UP / DOWN / NEUTRAL calls on 55 liquid assets, scored against realized prices after 5–7 days, with prompts and models frozen and hashed before collection. Across 230 scored predictions (29 Aug – 3 Oct 2026) the pipeline was 39.6% accurate under a ±2% neutral band, below always-DOWN (61.3%, a falling-market artifact), a coin flip (49.3%) and always-NEUTRAL (40.0%). The main reason is that it nearly always abstains: 85% of its calls are NEUTRAL, and those calls are correct at the base rate of flat outcomes (39.8% vs 40.0%). The 34 directional calls were 38.2% correct (95% CI 23.5–55.9%, p = 0.23); at this sample size only an edge of about 24 points over chance was detectable with 80% power. A pre-specified momentum-chasing hypothesis was half supported: the system followed the prior 3-day move in 62% of directional calls, but those moves did not reverse. In exploratory analyses, the committed calls were no more accurate than random subsets of predictions, and self-reported confidence was nearly constant (77% "medium"), suggesting that its abstention, which the prompt encouraged, did not track case-specific uncertainty. We find no evidence of edge, in a short, underpowered study of one falling-market window that stopped before its sample-size target.

detail.abstract: In the disruption of the digital machines business and marketing has changed. Marketing has seend numerous angles with the rise of digital systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an important technology in modern business promotion. Businesses use AI to understand customer behaviour, create advertisements, recommend products, communicate with customers, and improve marketing decisions. Traditional promotional methods often require significant time, money, and human effort. AI-based tools can help businesses automate repetitive tasks, identify potential customers, and deliver more relevant promotional messages. This research paper examines the role of AI in business promotion, its major applications, advantages, limitations, and future opportunities. It focuses on digital advertising, social media marketing, customer relationship management, predictive analytics, chatbots, and personalized marketing. The study follows a descriptive approach based on secondary sources. It concludes that AI can improve the efficiency and relevance of business promotion when used responsibly, with reliable data, customer trust, human supervision, and ethical practices.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being primarily an analytical technology to becoming an increasingly integrated component of marketing, customer engagement, advertising, and business promotion. Machine learning, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, conversational AI, and generative AI now support activities ranging from customer segmentation and campaign optimisation to content creation and personalised communication. This paper examines how AI is reshaping business promotion while critically evaluating whether technological capability necessarily translates into better marketing outcomes. The literature indicates that AI can improve the speed, scale, and analytical capacity of marketing decisions, particularly when organisations possess high-quality data and well-defined business processes. Evidence also shows that AI-assisted work can improve productivity in some settings, although effects vary considerably across workers and tasks. At the consumer level, personalisation can increase relevance and convenience, but excessive or opaque data use can reduce trust and create perceptions of surveillance. Generative AI presents a similar tension: it can substantially reduce content-production costs and increase creative output, while disclosure of fully automated content may reduce perceptions of brand authenticity. Case evidence from Netflix, Coca-Cola, and Klarna illustrates different approaches to AI-enabled promotion, ranging from recommendation systems to generative content and marketing automation. The paper argues that the central business question is therefore not whether firms should use AI, but where AI creates genuine customer and organisational value, where human judgement remains necessary, and what governance mechanisms are required to manage privacy, bias, misinformation, intellectual-property, and brand risks.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the mechanisms through which military leadership is generated in the Gulf states, using as its case the Commander-in-Chief of the Bahrain Defence Force, Field Marshal Sheikh Khalifa bin Ahmed Al Khalifa. It proceeds from the problem that dominant literatures on military leadership and civil-military relations remain captive to the Western model, and are therefore unable to explain how individual leadership is transformed into a stable sovereign pillar in a Gulf context where political legitimacy and professional competence are interwoven. The study proposes an original analytical framework-the "Triple Helix of Trust"-which explains institutional stability through the simultaneous generation of three levels of trust: vertical (political leadership-commander), horizontal (commander-officers and soldiers), and circumferential (military institution-society). Methodologically, the study adopts an analytical case study design, drawing on official documents, secondary analysis of Al-Qahtani (2018), and media documentation of the 2011 events and their aftermath. The study concludes that the philosophy of "silent deterrence" embodied by the Commander-in-Chief converts
military effectiveness into institutional stability, and that the 2011 test
constituted a critical juncture that demonstrated the durability of the
tripartite trust structure, making the Bahrain Defence Force a model of
military institutional resilience in the Gulf. The study's contribution lies
in elevating "trust" from a dependent variable in leadership literature to
a central explanatory mechanism, and in enriching the study of civil–
military relations in the Gulf states.

detail.abstract: China's 2025 reform of renewable pricing (Document 136) replaced administered tariffs for new wind and solar projects with provincial auctions for a two-sided contract for difference. Each province publishes a price ceiling, usually with a floor, and pays every selected project the highest accepted bid. This paper builds a source-linked register of the first provincial auction outcomes from official notices, archived copies and attributed reprints, coding the band, awarded price, procured and awarded volume, adequacy requirement and term, each tied to a quoted sentence of its source. The register is an availability-based sample: 32 auction groups in 15 of 31 provincial-level jurisdictions, of which 28 groups in 12 jurisdictions can be placed within their band. Most price bands rest on reprints rather than the issuing sites. Of the 28 classified groups, 21 cleared inside the band, 5 at the cap and 2 at the floor. Awards cluster high in the band, with a median position of 0.860 between floor and cap. The share of awarded volume at a band endpoint is dominated by one province and is reported only as a secondary statistic. We show that, because the band determines which bids are valid and, where an adequacy rule operates, procured volume is cut until valid bids exceed it by a required margin, an award at an endpoint identifies neither the price an unbounded auction would have produced nor bidders' costs, rents or conduct. Publishing initial and revised procured volume, valid submitted volume and bidder numbers alongside prices would make the auctions far easier to interpret.

detail.abstract: While AI adoption in organizational talent decisions has accelerated dramatically, systematic failures have emerged that existing "algorithmic bias" frameworks cannot fully explain: candidates silently excluded without traceability, well-intentioned diversity policies executed to their literal extreme, critical review steps "optimized" away by efficiency logic, and exceptional candidates systematically filtered out by historically derived success templates. This paper proposes the AI Organizational Magnifier Theory, which argues that AI systems do not independently generate organizational defects but amplify pre-existing structural capability gaps, unbounded standards, and decision consequences. The theory's meta-concept frames AI as a Brake Remover: an agent that dismantles three natural organizational braking mechanisms-the self-limiting nature of weak execution capability, the physical speed ceiling of human processing, and the temporal buffer of organizational friction. Drawing on practitioner research across 20 years and 16 Asia-Pacific markets, and four in-depth case studies, the theory identifies three pillars of amplification (structural, standards, consequence) and nine original sub-concepts. The paper proposes the governance axiom "Automate elimination; retain human judgment for selection" and the Verify the Tail mechanism, operationalized through a Three Gates governance framework. Three falsifiable predictions are offered for future empirical testing. The theory shifts AI ethics discourse from bias critique to structural diagnosis, and from moral exhortation to engineering governance.

detail.abstract: Cities play a crucial role in our societies and shape corporate actions in several ways. Their economic relevance poses an important policy question: Does the city in which the headquarters of a given company is located matter for its performance? If so, which urban dimensions matter more? We focus on the headquarters' location because it acts as the firm's central node of strategic, financial, and operational decisions, and a gateway to valuable resources. To date, no prior research has focused on this specific policy question, and no dominant paradigm exists to address it. Thus, we adopt a multilevel exploratory approach to inquire whether, and if so, how, the characteristics of a firm's home city-corresponding to where a firm locates its headquarters-relate to firm performance. To do so, we use a unique 2014-2016 panel of 27,933 firm-year observations of 9952 public firms based in 127 cities-located in the U.S., Europe, and Asia. Our findings show that the home city matters to firm performance and distinct dimensions of the home city play a different role across geographical areas and industries. Thus, our work highlights the growing importance of urban ecosystems in shaping firm outcomes and provides new insights for policymakers and international business scholars.

detail.abstract: Problem Definition: Despite the potential to capture additional demand through free on-demand fulfillment, few retailers offer such services because they require substantial upfront investment. The "Airbnb of Warehousing" (AW) offers a potential solution by allowing retailers to access excess fulfillment capacity from independent warehouses closer to their markets. We examine whether and how retailers should leverage AW's fulfillment flexibility to expand into on-demand markets. Methodology/Results: To answer this question, we propose a hybrid inventory strategy that combines centralized inventory with the AW, and we show that this approach can support efficient on-demand market expansion via the AW improving on the two benchmark strategies: pure centralized fulfillment and pure AW-based fulfillment. We use techniques from robust inventory management. We first characterize the AW business model and then derive robust inventory policies to support efficient on-demand market expansion through AW. For retailers with unknown on-demand markets prior to entry, we propose a hybrid strategy with a robust learning policy at the intersection of robust optimization and Bayesian inference under which retailers can flexibly learn their on-demand markets while minimizing the worst-case mismatch costs. On a test bed constructed with data from a leading AW platform, we show that the hybrid strategy can significantly increase retailers' expected profit relative to a pure centralized benchmark, and that these gains are larger in markets with less demand variability. Moreover, in markets with higher demand variability, the hybrid strategy outperforms a pure AW-based fulfillment strategy, which highlights the role of centralized facilities in cost-efficiently absorbing demand fluctuations through risk pooling, which AWs alone cannot efficiently handle. Managerial implications: Our proposed policies are robust to distributional assumption errors and can help retailers decide whether to expand into previously untapped on-demand markets, as well as how to do so efficiently through the AW.

detail.abstract: In the transition to a circular economy, resource recovery, product lifespan extension, and sustainable development orientation in supplier evaluation and selection are increasingly important, not only in academia but also in practical businesses. However, the intellectual structure, thematic development, and future research prospects of the circular supplier selection model are not yet fully integrated. This study presents a bibliographic analysis of 140 articles and reviews in English-language journals published between 2005 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus. We performed an analysis of publication growth rates, leading authors, countries, organizations, sources, and citation types using Biblioshiny and mapped the concurrent occurrence of keywords and topics over time using VOSviewer. The results show an annual publication growth rate of 20.34%, with 65% of the literature published between 2021 and 2025. The most productive countries were Iran and China, the most productive author was Hassan Mina, and the Journal of Cleaner Production was the leading source. Through keyword analysis, six thematic groups were identified, linking circular economy, supplier selection, closed-loop supply chains, sustainability, reverse logistics, and quantitative decision-making methods. The thematic development shows a shift from vague reverse logistics and supplier evaluation to circular economy, sustainability, and integrated supply chain management. However, there is still a lack of literature on artificial intelligence, dynamic supplier evaluation, specific criteria for circularity, and empirical evidence from emerging economies. The findings identified provide structured knowledge for both researchers and practitioners wishing to develop cyclical supplier selection theory and decision support systems.

detail.abstract: Cybersecurity is increasingly recognised as a socio-technical problem shaped by cultural, behavioural, and organisational factors, as well as technical controls, commonly referred to as Human Factors. As a result, organisations are establishing Security Champion programmes in which non-security staff encourage safe behaviour within their teams; though widespread, these initiatives too often lack a theoretical foundation and strategic integration. This paper synthesises 67 peer-reviewed studies on cybersecurity, behavioural science, organisational theory, and social network analysis (SNA), following PRISMA guidelines. The findings show that Champions mainly influence behaviour through informal networks defined by trust, peer education, and role-setting; they serve as cultural brokers who translate policy and affirm entrenched norms, with success augmented by leadership support, self-efficacy, and institution-based trust. Gaps remain, including a scarcity of longitudinal studies, limited integration between behavioural and network research methods, and a lack of measures consistent across studies. To address these gaps, the review lays the groundwork for a Security Champion Influence Model (SCIM) that combines behavioural determinants, trust, and network placement to increase Champions' impact.

Operational figures are drawn from the organisation's internal records, reported as audited by a local chartered accountant, while the qualitative account is based on field observations and interviews. detail.abstract: This study examined the impact of employee training and skills development on the technical competency and production performance of 12-coin press machine operators. Using a quantitative one-group pretest-posttest design, competency was assessed in CPM operation, autonomous maintenance and troubleshooting, and machine setup and conversion, while performance was measured through production output, downtime, and rejection rate. Results showed that overall competency increased from 3.12 to 3.98 (p < 0.001). Production output increased by 11.13%, while the downtime and rejection rate decreased by 29.51% and 22.99%, respectively. Although competency improvement was not significantly correlated with individual performance improvement, the findings indicate that training was associated with significant and operationally meaningful gains. Continuous competency-based training, standardized procedures, and regular performance monitoring are recommended.

detail.abstract: This study examines the factors influencing the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) outputs among professionals in Bangkok, as well as differences across demographic and employment characteristics. Grounded in technology acceptance and task-technology fit theories, an online questionnaire surveyed 644 working professionals between September and October 2026. Content validity was evaluated by three experts using the item-objective congruence index, and the overall instrument demonstrated high internal consistency, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.906. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and stepwise multiple linear regression. Stepwise regression identified seven significant predictors of adoption, i.e., perceived usefulness, task-technology fit, attitude, customization of outputs, user satisfaction, management support, and availability of resources, with perceived usefulness and task-technology fit showing the strongest predictive influence. In addition, adoption varied significantly by gender, age, education, usage duration, usage frequency, and job sector, but not by job position. Organizations aiming to integrate GenAI should emphasize direct task alignment, support output customization, and provide visible managerial backing, particularly during early user onboarding.

detail.abstract: The Arctic Circle and the lunar south pole share six structural constraints — energy scarcity, extreme-environment engineering requirements, autonomous systems dependency, capital intensity with long amortization timelines, governance sensitivity, and logistical vulnerability — that together produce equivalent economic behavior. Despite this structural equivalence, U.S. policy treats these domains as separate investment problems, allocating through distinct agency budgets, regulatory frameworks, and program offices. China, by contrast, appears to operate across both domains through a unified developmental axis — the Polar Silk Road as proof of concept for lunar-scale extreme-environment industrialization (see Section 4 for the evidence and its limits). This paper proposes the Polar-Lunar Continuum as a research framework with two defining criteria: two domains form a unified geoeconomic theater when (1) they share the six structural constraints and (2) the same capital-allocation logic applies to both. These criteria are treated here as a stipulated definition, not as a proposition claimed to be derived or proved. We present evidence from Arctic infrastructure commitments, projected cislunar economy valuations, China’s integrated Polar-Silk-tolunar strategy, and U.S. institutional fragmentation. We propose an evaluation matrix for program officers and investors to score dual-domain applicability, and a case for an International ExtremeEnvironment Infrastructure Bank (IEEIB) as the institutional vehicle for unified investment.

detail.abstract: Import cost shocks propagate through wholesale and retail markets before affecting consumer demand, but conventional linear and fixed-threshold models inadequately capture asymmetric price adjustments and substitution responses. This study develops a four-layer transmission model linking customs landed costs (CIF), wholesale prices, retail prices, and sales volumes. The framework combines competition indicators, price-adjustment frequency, adjustment inactivity, and shock direction with an adaptive threshold algorithm. Threshold selection integrates regime sample-balance constraints, bootstrap stability testing, and local refinement, while competition conditions and adjustment costs dynamically modify error-correction coefficients. Regime-specific price changes are passed to an Almost Ideal Demand System to estimate substitution patterns and income-group heterogeneity. The analysis uses weekly US customs, wholesale, and retail observations covering three import-dependent consumer goods categories, 64 geographic markets, 89,000 stock-keeping units, and 542 weeks from 2016 to 2026. Changes to low-value parcel customs rules in 2025 provide an identification shock. The optimal threshold is 4.6%, and linearity is rejected at the 1% level. Long-run pass-through elasticity reaches 0.68; positive and negative error-correction coefficients are-0.312 and-0.117, corresponding to half-lives of 0.43 and 1.28 months. Greater private-label penetration and lower adjustment costs moderate asymmetry. A 10% retail price increase reduces sales volume by 14.2%, with approximately 60% of displaced demand shifting toward domestic substitutes. Price elasticities are-1.94 for the lowest income quintile and-0.87 for the highest. The full model achieves 2.63% RMSE and 0.834 regime-classification F1, supporting its ability to capture asymmetric cost transmission and heterogeneous demand effects across markets with differing competitive conditions.

detail.abstract:
The household rule that money must be earned or borrowed before spending governs
almost every economic actor: families, businesses, cities, states, territories, and countries
that borrow in currencies they do not issue. This paper argues that it does not govern a
government that issues its own currency, lets it float, and owes mainly in that currency.
Such a government cannot be forced to run out of the money it issues, although it can still
default through legal or political failure.
The paper sets out how federal payments actually work, why the issuer and user positions
differ, and why that difference does not make spending free. A currency issuer's binding
limits are real resources, inflation, distribution, external purchasing power, and the
competence of its institutions. The paper takes up the strongest objections in turn: debt
and future generations, foreign creditors, inflation and hyperinflation, interest rates and
the dollar, crowding out, Ricardian equivalence, and the anchor for the price level.
It distinguishes the mechanical description associated with Modern Monetary Theory from
the policy programs its economists favor, and proposes that budget practice judge
proposals by the real resources they require. The paper summarizes a book-length
treatment.

detail.abstract: Do more economically successful parents have a stronger influence on their children? This paper empirically tests whether the economic achievement of parents is associated with greater similarity in norms and values between them and their children. I use data from the German SocioEconomic Panel (SOEP) survey and document several findings. detail.abstract:
Reproducibility in empirical finance is normally measured by what a paper says: whether it claims code is available, and whether a link appears. That is a property of the manuscript, not of the research. This paper measures the property that matters to anyone who wants to build on published work, by taking the released artifacts and attempting to run them.

We introduce the Reproducibility Attrition Ladder, an ordered scale of eleven cumulative rungs running from "the paper makes no code-availability claim" to "an emitted number matches the paper's headline result". Every rung except the last is decided mechanically, and every failure is recorded against a closed vocabulary of reasons, so the point at which an artifact stops, and the reason it stops, are both reportable as data rather than as anecdote. We apply the ladder to a corpus of arXiv quantitative-finance machine-learning papers, cloning each advertised repository, building its declared environment inside a container, and executing its entry point under a fixed time budget.

Applied to 459 arXiv quantitative-finance machine-learning papers that advertise a code repository, the curve falls steeply and not where the reproducibility discourse usually points. Link rot removes 4.4%. The two large losses are environment declaration, where 180 of 432 cloned repositories ship no dependency specification at all, and environment construction, where 110 of the 252 that declare dependencies can no longer install them, through packages that have left the index, pin sets that no longer resolve, and sources that no longer compile. Fifteen point five percent yield an identifiable entry point and seven papers, 1.5%, execute to completion and emit output without correspondence, manual repair, or reading beyond the README. Adjudicating those seven by hand against the papers' own claims leaves one that regenerated a published table, verified cell by cell; the rest emitted a self-test, an error, or an analysis run on data that never arrived. That single match depends on the looser of our two entry-point rules and on stored model outputs committed to the repository, and under the stricter rule the adjudicated count is zero rather than one, so the top of the ladder is reported as a bound and not as a rate. The earlier and smaller sample against which these figures might have been checked is nested inside this one and was scored by an earlier version of the harness, so it supports no claim of generality; on the 305 papers added since, the two large drops differ by 1.5 and 4.5 percentage points, and we show that even that agreement is partly an artifact of differing age composition.

The contrast with the existing finance result is the point. Running the code of 168 coordinated research teams on supplied raw data reproduces the published answer 52% of the time (Pérignon et al., 2024); starting instead from the URL a published paper gives its readers, with no data supplied and no author contact, 2.8% of artifacts run, and 1.5% emit output. Most of what computational reproducibility measures in finance depends on conditions an ordinary reader does not have.

The finding is about artifacts rather than findings: released code that does not run unassisted is not thereby wrong, but it cannot be checked without reimplementation. Artifacts from earlier cohorts build markedly less often than recent ones, but a single cross-section cannot separate aging from improving practice, and we report the gradient without claiming the mechanism.

The measurement instrument is itself released as an installable package, so the study can be repeated on other corpora, re-run as the literature changes, and extended to fields beyond finance. We are explicit about what the ladder does and does not establish: an artifact that fails to run is not thereby wrong, it is not independently executable as released, which is a weaker but more precisely measurable claim.

detail.abstract: Broadband policy in the United States treats the digital divide largely as a problem of availability, most visible in rural places where infrastructure is absent. This paper documents a complementary urban divide of performance: in low-income urban neighborhoods where service is mapped as available, the connectivity students actually receive falls persistently short of federal benchmarks. The evidence comes from myQoI ("my quality of internet"), an application on the district-issued laptops of the Fresno Unified School District that runs automated speed tests off campus, resolves each measurement to an individual student, and counts each student once. Of the 58,520 students enrolled in grades 1-12, 27.1% have no off-campus measurement on the district device. Among the 42,603 students with eligible measurements, the median student experiences 60 Mbps down and 14.5 Mbps up, and 78.3% fall below at least one component of the 100/20 Mbps standard; under a recurring-download classification, only 10.1% of measured students (7.4% of enrolled students) are well-served. Upload is the binding constraint, and it is structured by provider: students whose primary provider is the dominant cable incumbent have a median upload of 11 Mbps, against 148.5 Mbps for students on fiber. Linked to the same students' engagement and achievement records, connectivity shows modest associations that do not hold up under matching and weighting designs. The central contribution is an institutional measurement architecture, repeated automated tests from a managed fleet of end-user devices resolved to individuals, that makes an urban performance divide visible where availability-based mapping cannot, and that anchor institutions could adopt to supply independent evidence to broadband policy.

detail.abstract: This study tests whether growth, value, momentum, and undervalued stocks can outperform the S&P 500 over a five year period when the starting conditions are favorable, based on prior research. Stock selection was based on factors including price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, interest rates, and previous stock market performance. The average percentage return of each category was compared with the S&P 500 over the same five-year period. The results show that growth stocks achieved an average return of 388.22%, outperforming the S&P 500 return of 89.80%. This study provides insight into the performance of different stock selection strategies and may help investors better understand the limitations of relying on a single investment strategy.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence and robotics may reduce the human labour that production technically requires well before they reduce the labour that firms employ. This paper develops a taskbased model that makes that distinction precise and derives its consequences. Tasks are allocated between workers and machines by comparative advantage; a technological frontier determines which tasks machines can perform, and the cost of machine capacity determines which of those tasks they do perform. The gap between the two defines the Labour Necessity Ratio, λ, which equals the share of human-performed task content that lies beyond the frontier. Three results follow that do not emerge from any of the constructs separately. First, when machine cost rather than capability binds, technical progress accumulates as a latent stock, visible in λ but invisible in employment, wages and productivity statistics; the economy remains on its cost-efficient frontier while λ falls. Second, λ measured today predicts the share of core jobs that survive once machine costs fall far enough to adopt the existing frontier, exactly when product demand is unit-elastic and with an explicit correction otherwise. Third, when displaced workers can take residual low-productivity work, the strain of automation appears first as falling wage adequacy (κ) with stable employment, and employment contracts only when residual wages reach an institutional floor; the floor, social insurance and ownership arrangements determine whether the same technological shock produces a working-poor, an unemployment or a shared-ownership trajectory. The sequence survives, and strengthens, when wages are market-determined, because wage compression slows automation and rebuilds the latent stock. When institutional protection depends on workers' bargaining power, and that power falls with necessity, all configurations converge on the working-poor trajectory except broad ownership of automated capital. The Adaptation Gap is defined in common units, as the rate at which the automatable share of the task window grows net of new-task creation. An application to autonomous driving, using California disengagement reports for 2015 to 2020, illustrates how the boundary specification of the minimum labour requirement is made operational and how λ can diverge from employment by several orders of magnitude before employment changes. United States wage data for May 2025, benchmarked against living wages, give κ empirical content and support the model's assumption about residual work. Evidence from 702 US occupations between 2019 and 2025 shows that, since late 2022, employment has grown more slowly in occupations more exposed to large language models, with no relative fall in their wages and no comparable pattern before 2022. This is consistent with the model's core-sector mechanism under institutionally set wages.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations and increasing pressure on urban infrastructure have accelerated the development of smart cities driven by advanced digital technologies. Among these technologies, remote sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) have emerged as critical tools for enhancing urban management, sustainability, and resilience. This paper is a narrative review of the integration of remote senåsing technologies and AI techniques in managing smart cities, focusing on their applications in urban planning, transportation management, environmental monitoring, disaster risk reduction, energy optimization, and public safety. The synthesis draws on a purposively selected body of peer-reviewed literature and on sixteen real-world urban case studies spanning six continents, complemented by recent open-data indicators for the corresponding countries; it does not follow a systematic-review search protocol, and its coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive. Remote sensing supplies large-scale, multi-temporal geospatial data through satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)—typically periodic rather than continuous—which are increasingly combined with in-situ Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensor networks, while AI enables data processing, predictive analytics, pattern recognition, and decision support. The study discusses methodological frameworks that combine geospatial data analytics with machine learning and deep learning models to support urban governance. It further examines major challenges associated with data integration, computational complexity, privacy concerns, governance issues, and economic constraints, and explores emerging trends—including digital twins, edge computing, and explainable AI—as future directions. The review concludes that the synergistic integration of remote sensing and AI offers substantial potential for improving urban sustainability, operational efficiency, and resilience, while cautioning that most of the reviewed evidence is drawn from individual case studies whose demonstrated effects are not yet established across cities.

detail.abstract: An unchanged policy rate does not imply an unchanged economic judgment. detail.abstract: Despite the established link between oil rent and economic growth, the moderating effect of institutional quality and access to finance on the relationship between oil rent and economic wellbeing remains unexplored. This study examines the effect of oil rent on economic well-being in Nigeria-a country that is both a net oil exporter and net-importer of petroleum products. We also examine how the relationship is influenced by the quality of governance institutions and access to finance during the 1996 to 2021 period. We find that oil rent improves economic well-being in Nigeria through higher GDP per capita growth, economic growth and low unemployment. Institutional quality enhances the contribution of oil rent to economic well-being by decreasing the level of unemployment in Nigeria. Access to finance through bank branch expansion did not translate oil rent into positive economic well-being. There is a uni-directional granger causality between oil rent and GDP per capita growth, GDP growth rate and unemployment rate. The findings call on policymakers to increase oil rent due to its significant role in improving economic well-being. They should strengthen governance institutions by introducing laws and policies that protect public interests and combat corruption in the petroleum sector to increase oil rent and its positive trickle-down effect on people. Policymakers also need to identify other appropriate mechanisms for broadening access to finance to members of the public who need financing to access the infrastructure and products that were built using oil wealth such as schools and hospitals. This perspective extends beyond the conventional focus on net oil-exporting economies and provides a fresh contribution to the resource curse debate.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic model of common-pool resource management under uncertainty about spatial migration patterns. A renewable resource is distributed across two patches, and non-cooperative harvesters are uncertain about self-retention and dispersal rates. In a cooperative benchmark, internalizing both spatial and informational externalities can even raise total extraction relative to the non-cooperative equilibrium by avoiding redundant information provision. The analysis highlights the institutional value of coordinating both spatial management and information production for mobile resources.

detail.abstract: The doctoral dissertation “The Choice of Exchange Rate Mechanisms in Vietnam’s Macroeconomic Policy” by Nguyen Hoang Giang was successfully defended at Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City. The study examines the theoretical and practical foundations of exchange rate regimes, reviews the evolution of Vietnam’s exchange rate policy, and proposes an appropriate exchange rate mechanism for the country's economic development and international integration. A major contribution of the dissertation is its analysis of exchange rate policy as a strategic macroeconomic tool rather than merely a monetary instrument. The research demonstrates that the choice of an exchange rate regime has significant implications for inflation control, international trade, foreign investment, balance of payments stability, and overall macroeconomic performance. Based on theoretical analysis and international experience, the dissertation recommends a managed floating exchange rate regime for Vietnam, combining market signals with necessary government intervention to maintain economic stability and competitiveness. Issues such as the coordination of exchange rate policy with monetary policy, inflation management, external balance, foreign exchange market development, and flexible exchange rate management continue to be central concerns in Vietnam’s macroeconomic governance today. The dissertation therefore retains both academic significance and practical value for policymakers and researchers.

detail.abstract: People are turning to AI assistants more frequently to tell them what to do with their money. Sometimes this is because they simply cannot afford a human adviser. The obvious worry is that the model will make computation errors. We show that with complete inputs, frontier models seldom violate basic financial principles, and increasingly warn about the ones that are applicable. The real behavioural risk is that the appropriateness of AI advice for a given person hinges on facts that only that person knows, and people do not know what matters. In an oracle-anchored audit of four frontier models across three standard personal-finance decisions, we fix the person and vary the question. If the user asks a natural, under-specified question that omits the one fact that makes the difference in their case, the confident advice of these models is wrong for that person in 33/33 cases - for example, telling a user to "pay off your credit card" when that card is already at 0% and the person lacks an emergency fund, or "pay down your loan" when the person is missing a 100% employer match. Adding that one fact results in the same models making the correct choice in 11/11 cases. Advice from an under-specified prompt is generally correct for control personas whose situation matches the model's default assumption, so the error is not model inability but the interaction between under-specified input and a fact that goes against the default. The user, however, cannot provide what they do not know is pertinent. In an exploratory pilot (N=21), 76% did not notice an AI plan that quietly wasted half of an employer match, and 62% said they would follow it. As models become more fluent and confident, this dependence on input is hidden rather than resolved, because fluency makes the output seem complete. We interpret this through omission neglect, audit studies of advice, and research on advice-taking under low expertise, and argue that the key safeguard is structured elicitation of decision-flipping facts together with output that can be audited. The evidence is preliminary: the machine study is a small oracle-anchored demonstration and the human study is an exploratory pilot, which motivates a preregistered, powered experiment.

detail.abstract: The structural change in the European Union (EU) involves a decline in the number of holdings and a transformation of farming systems. This study examines the territorial dimensions of this process using data from the 2010 and 2020 Agricultural Censuses and the Territorial Shift Share Analysis method. The analysis compares changes at the EU-27, Member State, and NUTS 2 regional levels to assess the contributions of EU central, national, and regional trends, without identifying specific causal mechanisms. The study uses three scenarios-status quo, optimistic, and pessimistic-to project the number of farms by 2030. The results indicate that, compared to 2020, the number of holdings could decrease by 16% under the basic scenario and by 33% under the pessimistic scenario, whereas the optimistic scenario projects a slight increase of 1%. The territorial analysis attributes 61% of the projected change to the EU level and 39% to national and regional factors, although their relative contributions vary across Member States. These findings highlight the wide-ranging yet spatially uneven nature of structural changes in agricultural holdings, as well as the importance of accounting for the differences between EUlevel trends and national and regional contexts when interpreting agricultural transformations and their implications for policy and sustainable development.

detail.abstract: I study informational efficiency at the level of the individual contract in prediction markets, using a frozen dataset of 244 resolved Kalshi markets (21 distinct events, 2024-2026) in high-emotion categories. Three sets of results emerge. First, naive trading strategies fail: contrarian mean-reversion loses significantly even under event-clustered inference (mean return per unit staked-0.38, 95% CI [-0.67,-0.05];-0.49 with taker fees and bid-ask execution), momentum is statistically indistinguishable from zero yet ruinous under Kelly compounding, and the market price itself is a strong benchmark (Brier 0.072 at two-thirds of contract life versus 0.156 for the climatological forecast; skill +0.54). Second, efficiency is measurable ex post: I construct a composite contract-level efficiency index (convergence skill, variance-ratio resistance, random-walk-normalized signal-to-noise), whose category ranking is robust to the choice of weights (Spearman ≥ 0.95 across nine weighting schemes). Third, efficiency is not predictable ex ante: none of 13 canonical efficiency metrics predicts out-of-sample under event-grouped cross-validation and Bonferroni correction-the single apparent signal is shown to be a mechanical artifact, both by synthetic-market controls and in closed form (expected calibrated surprise equals 2√(p(1-p)))-and none of 18 pre-registered indicator-target tests for regime transitions passes. Exploratory analyses indicate that contract-level efficiency is multidimensional (first principal component: 40% of variance) and continuously distributed (no bimodality), consistent with the Adaptive Markets Hypothesis. Code, data, and the pre-registration protocol are available for full reproduction.

detail.abstract: This research analyses the financial interdependence and the transmission mechanisms of volatility shocks between eight African stock markets and the global market in the context of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Daily data covering the period from 1 January 2018 to 1 August 2026 are used, with the FTSE All-World index as the international benchmark. The empirical strategy combines several complementary approaches: CCC-GARCH and DCC-GARCH models, wavelet coherence, cross-quantilograms, and the connectedness methodology of Diebold and Yilmaz (2012). The results reveal heterogeneity in financial dependence, with dynamic conditional correlation observed mainly in South Africa and Morocco. However, the cross-quantilograms show no statistically significant change in directional dependence between the pre-crisis and stress periods, which does not allow us to confirm the existence of contagion in the strict sense. Moreover, the total connectedness index, estimated at about 14.97%, indicates moderate overall connectivity. Thus, world market, South Africa and the BRVM are the main net transmitters of volatility, while Kenya, Nigeria and Tunisia appear as net receivers. The insensitivity of the total connectedness index (TCI) to changes in the observation window and in the sample attests to the robustness of the results.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the mechanisms and conditions underlying negative convexity in pass-through mortgage-backed securities (MBSs) backed by fixed-rate mortgages. We first derive an exact decomposition of MBS prices into three components: the present value of interest-rate-independent cash flows, the present value of principal repaid early through interest-rate-dependent prepayments, and an interest rate option component capturing the reduction in future cash flows due to prepayments. Under a first-order approximation, the latter two components resemble portfolios of floorlets and Asian-style interest rate options, respectively. We then apply a cumulant expansion to derive closed-form valuation approximations under the one-factor Hull--White model. Numerical results show that including the second cumulant improves accuracy relative to a first-cumulant approximation. Building on the price decomposition, we decompose duration and convexity into component-level contributions and express the condition for negative convexity in terms of their second-order interest rate sensitivities. Finally, phase diagrams across interest rate levels and refinancing sensitivities identify the regions where negative convexity occurs and the corresponding sign boundaries. The negative-convexity region expands as the long-run mean of refinancing sensitivity increases. Negative convexity can arise even when no refinancing incentive exists initially, while its magnitude may vary nonmonotonically with the interest rate level. These findings explain negative MBS convexity through the sensitivities of its price components and quantitatively characterize the conditions governing its occurrence.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we explored some of the most significant ways that religious themes present themselves in video games. Our analysis covered multiple games, but The Binding of Isaac remained a core part of the paper due to how tightly its religious messaging is interwoven with its mechanics and story. While analyzing the games in question, we classified them in 3 different categories: religion as background, as narrative, and as a vessel to impart a specific message. These categories were based on prior research about religion in games, however, we found them to be more fluid than originally classified, as the featured games frequently overlap rather than exclude each category, with The Binding of Isaac being a great representation of this. The most significant examples that we found are those where religious themes interact with other parts of the game, such as its story, rather than those with the most imagery. Finally, we echoed previous findings that the religions represented in the current zeitgeist of games are largely skewed towards Christianity.

detail.abstract: Two old market sayings hold that news is already priced in by the time it is published, and that the rumor is bought while the news is sold. Both are empirical claims about event time: they place the price move associated with a piece of news before and at publication rather than after it. Whether the claims hold, for which kinds of news, and by how much are basic questions about how fast markets absorb public information. We test them on 4.57 million financial news articles covering roughly 3,000 US stocks (2023-2026). A large language model teacher, distilled into a compact classifier through active learning, assigns each article one of 17 event tags and five attributes; articles are clustered into stories to separate first reports from follow-up coverage; and beta-adjusted abnormal returns are measured around the resulting 1.68 million stock-day events, with 364,405 neutral-sentiment events as a placebo group. Three results follow. First, the price move associated with news concentrates before and at publication: pooled across all signed events, the cumulative move in the news direction by the close of publication day is 2.8 times its value twenty days later, and for rumor-flagged events the directional return is concentrated around the rumor event, with little incremental return at the subsequent linked non-rumor event. Second, measured against the placebo of comparable stocks, markets underreact to numbers and overreact to stories: quantified fundamental news (earnings, dividends, guidance, analyst actions) keeps drifting in the direction of the news for weeks, while soft story-driven news (launches, macro commentary, leadership) gives back its move. Third, news carries width as well as direction: neutral news raises publication-day volatility. The study also produces a table of measured drift for each event tag, usable as a prior in news-conditioned forecasting models.

detail.abstract: When a large language model recommends a financial action, whose risk appetite does it use? We combine a ten-item taxonomy of AI biases in financial decisions, behavioural experiments on open-weight models and measurements inside one model. In hosted models, a 623-word persona moved GPT-4.1's risky choices from 2.8% to 95.6% in runs that always listed the safe option first. On open weights, the same tasks with neutral option labels show that such a persona mainly weakens the pull towards the first-listed option: a length-matched cautious persona has the same effect, and no condition responds to expected value. In a financial allocation test rerun from its original prompts, the raw choices of every open model follow the answer labels. Scoring each item in all four combinations of label and position separates a pull towards a letter from a pull towards a position; the two can offset each other and do not add up, so the usual two-order debiasing misleads. Qwen3's apparently mandate-sensitive preference shrinks to about 8 points of expected return, against about 200 for the letter, and to about 1 point with neutral labels. Inside Qwen2.5, surface features are readable from the first block, news sentiment, sector knowledge and asset riskiness in the middle blocks, and the answer forms only at the end; the model encodes asset riskiness with 96% accuracy but answers correctly about half the time. Lesions show that the first block is vital, and steering along a mandate direction moves the answer letter, not the investment. We translate the evidence into four governance gates: specify, validate, calibrate, and release and monitor.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between corruption and tax revenue mobilization in developing countries, emphasizing the role of different institutional sources of corruption. Using panel data for 122 low-and middle-income countries over the period 1990-2017, the analysis combines tax revenue data from the ICTD Government Revenue Dataset with corruption indicators from V-Dem and the Worldwide Governance Indicators. A two-step system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimator is employed to account for the dynamic nature of tax revenues and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal a negative and statistically significant relationship between aggregate corruption and total, direct, and indirect tax revenues. Disaggregated estimates further indicate that executive, publicsector, judicial, legislative, and regime corruption are all negatively associated with tax revenue mobilization, although the magnitude of these associations varies across institutional dimensions and tax categories. The results suggest that indirect taxation may be particularly vulnerable to certain forms of corruption, especially executive, public-sector, and regime corruption. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between institutional sources of corruption when analyzing fiscal performance and designing policies aimed at strengthening domestic revenue mobilization.

detail.abstract: Several synthetic-dollar protocols take stablecoin deposits and lend them to companies that operate GPU clusters. The hardware, borrowers' revenues and loan agreements are off-chain, while loan and vault transactions are recorded on a public chain. Protocol-hosted metadata describes about 4,560 pledged GPUs at 66.8% stated loan-to-value, but does not independently establish custody or realizable collateral value. detail.abstract: The current speed of the AI revolution is a serious matter. Even with grave risks, the ultimate question is not whether to accelerate or decelerate. It’s where we are going. What is the purpose of AI, its telos? AI company leaders have called for human flourishing to be this north star, but often have conceptually “thin” frameworks, leading to unforeseen risks and missed opportunities in AI design and governance. To date, there has been little concrete discussion within the AI arena of what such flourishing actually looks like. To address this challenge, we develop an interdisciplinary definition and a “thicker” framework of what it means for humans to live and do well, centered on values and ends that people seek, develop, and attain through their capabilities. It offers a systemic, pluralistic account of influencers that shape flourishing and facilitators that serve as contextual drivers (e.g., families, local ecologies) of individual flourishing and constituents of the common good. We draw from the value ethics and virtue ethics traditions and global scientific studies of well-being. As a case example, we apply the framework to one value, one capability, one influencer, and one facilitator. Practically, human capabilities provide a “tractable” way to measure the impact of AI on human flourishing beyond user engagement or satisfaction. We conclude with a “whole-of-society” method for using this research to empower families and communities, improve engineering practices, innovate business models, and strengthen AI policy.

detail.abstract: The growing demand for transparent and reliable corporate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions data has led to the emergence of large public climate databases designed to support research, financial decision-making, and public policy. Among these, the Climate Data Utility (CDU, formerly the Net-Zero Data Public Utility, NZDPU) has rapidly become an important source of harmonized corporate climate information. This study evaluates the reliability of CDU GHG emissions data by systematically comparing it with the corresponding raw disclosures collected by the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), one of the world’s largest global repositories of corporate climate information. Using a company-year matching procedure combining exact identifier matching and fuzzy string matching, we align more than 9,780 companies that reported between 2018 and 2024 and compare emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2 (location-based and market-based), and Scope 3 categories. Our results show that CDU reproduces reported emissions with a relatively high level of consistency for Scope 1 and Scope 2 location-based emissions, where exact agreement reaches approximately 54% and increases to nearly 74% when allowing a ±10% tolerance. Scope 2 market-based and Scope 3 emissions exhibit lower exact agreement and greater observation-level variability. Distributional analyses nevertheless indicate strong overall correlations between CDU and CDP across all emission scopes. Overall, our findings indicate that CDU constitutes a reliable secondary source for large-scale empirical analyses, benchmarking exercises, and cross-sectional studies based on corporate climate disclosures. However, researchers should exercise greater caution when conducting company-level analyses involving Scope 3 emissions. This study offers a practical guidance for researchers and practitioners relying on the CDU climate data infrastructure, likely destined to grow in the future.

detail.abstract: This paper measures what retail traders get back per unit staked on three crypto venues and sets it against what gamblers get back at six casino games, five with exactly known payout laws and a popular slot priced at its published return. The venues are pump.fun memecoins on Solana (44,114,785 retail positions held by 6,693,737 wallets), Hyperliquid perpetual futures (5,193,148 trading episodes from 247,545 wallets) and Polymarket prediction markets (21,428,139 positions from 327,866 wallets), each rebuilt from on-chain records for the six weeks from 8 August to 18 September 2026 and each tested with the same pre-registered statistics. Retail memecoin traders get back 0.754 per unit staked (95% interval 0.726 to 0.777), less than American roulette (0.947), the Sweet Bonanza slot (0.965) or any other game in the comparison. Only 14.1% of memecoin wallets finish the window ahead, whereas gamblers placing the same stakes finish ahead between 19.7% and 49.1% of the time depending on the game. Per unit of peak notional exposure, perpetual futures retail get back 0.9999, and Polymarket retail get back 0.984, above both roulettes and the slot and level with the other games; on both venues the share of winners falls between the slots and the table games. Rebuilt the same way for two unregistered windows in 2024, memecoin retail got back 0.971 in August to September and between 0.921 and 0.984 in November to December, so the 2026 shortfall describes that market at that time rather than memecoins in general. Memecoin bets placed at a random time in a token's first day lack a slot machine's jackpot tail as well, since a bet returning 100 times its stake comes up about once in 250,000 tries. A permutation test that holds the trading day and the stake size fixed finds a skilled minority among memecoin and perpetual futures traders, clearly persistent on memecoins and only marginally on perpetual futures, but none among Polymarket retail wallets. On memecoins the wallets that reliably win are token creators (1.56 per unit staked, 95% interval 1.47 to 1.66), launch-block buyers (1.49) and a small group of very fast traders.

The findings suggest that peer-group design can affect valuation signals and historical portfolio outcomes. They do not establish uniform dominance, risk-adjusted alpha, causal effects, or independently replicated out-of-sample performance.

detail.abstract: The emergence of ex ante regulation of digital markets reshapes the relationship between economic knowledge and law in market governance. Unlike traditional competition law, where economic analysis is primarily used ex post to assess the effects of potentially anti-competitive conduct, digital regulation requires forward-looking assessments. detail.abstract: Conservation practices can generate ecosystem services beyond the environmental outcomes that motivate their adoption, but these co-benefits are rarely incorporated into evaluations of conservation investments. We estimate the recreational value of forested riparian buffers using a random utility model of fishing-site choice in Pennsylvania. Combining angler trip data with spatial information on Conservation Reserve Program buffers, water quality, land use, and other site characteristics, we estimate that anglers are willing to pay approximately $0.47 per trip for an additional acre of forested riparian buffer near a fishing site. This estimate is stable to the inclusion of observed site characteristics and remains positive across a range of alternative specifications and robustness analyses. Scaling per-trip values using population-level visitation implies seasonal recreational benefits of approximately $2,064 per additional acre at the mean fishing site and $1,073 at the median site, values that exceed annualized buffer-cost estimates considered in our analysis. These average benefits mask important spatial heterogeneity: the recreational value of additional buffer acreage is relatively high in landscapes with low to moderate agricultural intensity but declines as the agricultural share of the surrounding landscape increases. Our results demonstrate that local recreational benefits can constitute an economically important component of the returns to agricultural conservation and that their spatial incidence may differ from the downstream water-quality benefits that typically motivate buffer investments.

detail.abstract: This article develops an integrative conceptual framework for evaluating economic governance by connecting institutional independence, market contestability, inflation measurement, and distributional accountability. Although these domains represent well-established areas of economic scholarship, they are frequently evaluated through isolated analytical lenses. This study argues that a comprehensive assessment of public economic governance requires a systematic bridge between the quality of public evidence, the structural capacity of enforcing institutions, the competitive dynamics of markets, and the social distribution of policy consequences. Centering on this evaluation, the paper introduces the normative-analytical principle of "laic economics," defined as a procedural standard requiring binding public economic decisions to be justified through publicly examinable evidence, general legal standards, and transparent reasoning rather than privileged ideological or doctrinal authority. Methodologically, the study adopts a conceptual synthesis design, deriving bounded research propositions and exploring boundary conditions rather than reporting empirical econometric estimations. To illustrate the framework's operational value, the analysis applies an algebraic log-change decomposition to consumer price indicators, distinguishing short-term monthly price momentum and arithmetic base effects from causal macroeconomic drivers. Ultimately, the proposed model provides a multidimensional architecture to guide future comparative, countrylevel, and longitudinal research toward more accountable public economic justification.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a universal framework for peaceful coexistence grounded in reciprocal restraint: agents must refrain from imposing on others any condition they would not rationally accept under role reversal. Unlike traditional ethical systems organized around values, duties, or aggregate outcomes, this framework defines peace as a constraint system anchored in symmetry and non-imposition. Peace is further characterized as an ongoing relational achievement—a reproduced state requiring continuous recognition and enforcement, not merely a static equilibrium condition. Rationality is defined internally as the requirement of logical consistency under role reversal. Harm is operationalized as a non-consensual, threshold-level reduction in functional capacity across six domains, including a newly specified domain of Relational Integrity that captures the constitutive conditions of social participation. An Epistemic Asymmetry Corollary establishes that valid application of the role-reversal test under conditions of structural inequality requires evidence-seeking rather than imagination-substitution by structurally dominant agents. The framework addresses the structural distinction between peace maintenance and peace reconstitution, specifying what is required to rebuild peace as a social fact after significant disruption. It resolves both acts and omissions through a unified symmetry test, introduces a conflict-resolution mechanism for competing claims, specifies the class of cases that remain genuinely indeterminate, and incorporates scope conditions, enforcement requirements, epistemic limits, temporal harm, and collective agency. The result is a scalable, non-coercive model applicable to individuals, institutions, and across cultural contexts.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a mathematically rigorous, single-pass programmatic pipeline to solve a fifty year misspecification error in contingent claim analysis by extracting true underlying physical stock returns directly from option cross-sections. Traditionally, option finance relies on the Black-Scholes model, which holds the expected return of a stock constant and forces volatility to absorb all real world market noise-creating an artificial distortion known as the "volatility smile." This pipeline reverses that math. By holding volatility constant and treating the options chain as a closed financial system, we isolate an options-derived market rate. Operating on the raw, un-smoothed historical cross-section from the canonical Rubinstein and Gou datasets originally published in The Journal of Finance, we demonstrate that traditional pricing anomalies—namely the volatility smile and tail return degradation—are artificial distortions produced by a fundamental mixed-space coordinate error. By transforming the math into a scale-invariant coordinate framework based on option leverage weights, the pipeline naturally flattens these distortions. The model collapses the uncorrected tracking errors into an exceptionally tight, 15 basis-point flat band resting cleanly between 21.04% and 21.19% across the entire data chain. This establishes a generalized, reproducible computational method for asset return discovery that eliminates traditional pricing anomalies.

detail.abstract: Illicit financial flows (IFFs) are one of several global phenomena that bad actors have, for some time now, carried out under the veil of internet secrecy and within the encrypted recesses of deep web technologies. However, with the recent rise of social media and secure internet messaging platforms, scores of illicit transactions are now being conducted through open and accessible mainstream social media platforms. These transactions are happening at this very moment, right in front of our eyes. And as they occur and translate into massive outflows, the world continues to stand by and watch as the commonwealth of countries in the Global South is silently and untraceably siphoned. This essay is an exposé on how social media and creator platforms have become critically under-regulated channels for IFF transactions. Drawing from doctrinal legal analysis, news reports, press releases, enforcement records, and quantitative proxy data, this essay examines the three social platform typologies that facilitate illicit financial flows and how each of them uniquely collapses the three stages of money laundering into a single and untraceable transaction interface. The essay goes on to spotlight how mainstream social platforms have legally and structurally averted the anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing frameworks that govern traditional financial institutions. To address this menace, the essay details a top-down policy implementation proposal that spans across the supranational, national, sub-national, and corporate levels. The essay concludes with a bold caveat stating that until mainstream platforms are designated and regulated as international financial intermediaries, they will continue to serve as a conduit for laundering the commonwealth of Global South countries in plain sight.

detail.abstract: Constitutional frameworks can specify whether policies are admissible without specifying how constitutionally required corrections can be implemented without producing secondary instability. This paper develops the Constitutional Transition Simulation Framework, a structured, simulation-ready architecture for sequencing the correction, reversal, and reconstruction of policies under the constraints established by the Economic Constitution. The framework separates three analytically distinct problems: constitutional validity, execution feasibility, and institutional recognition viability. Constitutional requirements determine whether a policy is admissible; execution variables govern how authorized corrections can be implemented and sequenced; and a recognitional viability functional tracks whether the institutions responsible for constitutional evaluation retain the operative conditions required to perform that role. These layers are integrated through a precedence-preserving authorization and routing architecture that prevents implementation difficulty, political feasibility, or institutional recognition from altering constitutional verdicts. The framework further specifies system-boundary and policy-individuation requirements, uncertainty handling, adaptive sequencing, circuit breakers, causal certification, public constitutional translation, and framework-level review. A Public Constitutional Interface translates internal constitutional diagnostics without transferring adjudicatory authority to public-facing metrics, while recursive review provides an auditable mechanism for detecting degradation in the framework's own calibration and institutional operation. The resulting architecture treats constitutional transition as a dynamic sequencing problem rather than an endpoint comparison: a constitutionally admissible destination does not by itself establish that every pathway toward it is operationally viable. The framework therefore provides a formal basis for simulating policy correction while preserving constitutional precedence, institutional continuity, and systemic stability under conditions of uncertainty and interdependence.

detail.abstract: Can AI increase collective action from workers? To study this question I exploit a major event-shock: the advent of ChatGPT. I posit that the AI innovation incentivizes collective action via collective bargaining because workers anticipate a fall in their bargaining power after AI is implemented at the workplace. detail.abstract: Generative AI is putting the law of reverse engineering (RE) under severe strain. Existing IP and technology laws assume that RE is expensive and time-consuming, and that it requires specialized expertise. They generally allow it, but they rely on its difficulty as a filter to separate (permissible) RE from (impermissible) copying and theft. Generative AI is changing this equation by making RE much faster, cheaper, and easier. AI systems can identify hardware components, extract firmware, decompile object code, and clone entire apps. The resulting struggle between technology vendors and reverse engineers will challenge a wide range of laws, including trade secret, copyright, anti-circumvention, computer misuse, and contract. In this article, we describe the ways in which AI is changing RE, map these new practices onto existing laws, and sketch ways that the legal system could respond and their associated trade-offs.

detail.abstract: We characterize when one-step-ahead forecasts are consistent with Bayesian learning about a fixed, unknown outcome distribution. With two periods of data, a conditionally i.i.d. (CIID) representation exists if and only if the matrix of joint outcome probabilities is completely positive. For binary outcomes, this is equivalent to symmetry and reinforcement (observing an outcome cannot lower the next-period probability of that outcome).  For at most four outcomes, complete positivity is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness. These conditions can be tested using forecasts alone, without eliciting beliefs about the unknown distribution. Two-period forecasts cannot distinguish CIID learning from some forms of perceived persistence, but can reveal some forms of perceived reversal. For longer binary-outcome horizons, we give an explicit truncated-moment test and characterize the minimum support size of a rationalizing prior. With multiple periods and outcomes, the characterization uses count sufficiency, pairwise exchangeability, and complete positivity of the implied moment tensor.

detail.abstract: Does CBDC design determine whether digital currency stabilizes or destabilizes commercial banks? We embed a programmable CBDC in a global-game model of bank runs and establish three results. First, a frictionless CBDC raises equilibrium fragility: removing the conversion costs that once deterred strategic withdrawal enlarges the set of fundamentals over which self-fulfilling runs occur. Second, the Paradox of Friction: a pre-committed, state-contingent fee that escalates convexly with aggregate withdrawals can push run probability below the cash-regime level, because anticipating prohibitive fees during a panic weakens each depositor's incentive to flee. A numerical calibration places the run-probability gap between a frictionless and a programmable CBDC at 38 percentage points, rising to 46 at a 5% deposit premium. Third, continuous fee schedules dominate hard withdrawal caps, whose payoff discontinuities generate preemptive runs. Programmability, not digitization, is the critical design dimension for financial stability, and where conversion is blocked outright, quantity caps such as the holding limits proposed for the digital euro reproduce the destabilizing discontinuity we identify.

Excel remains central to health economic modeling, but decision-relevant defects are difficult to detect and auditing of HEOR workbooks with large language model (LLM) remains poorly characterized. We evaluated seeded-defect detection and separate-session repeatability of HEOR FAME, a structured, evidence-governed, capability-aware framework for LLM-assisted Excel-model auditing.

Methods. Two synthetic models—a three-state Markov cohort (>400,000 formula cells) and mixture-cure partitioned-survival model (PSM; >500,000)—were seeded with 26 and 28 defects and 8 and 9 unusual-but-correct decoys, respectively. Seven defects changed the base-case conclusion at $150,000 per quality-adjusted life-year gained. Both models were development benchmarks; framework revisions, however, contained no workbook-specific rules. Each seeded model underwent five audits in separate OpenAI Codex sessions (GPT6-Astra Max) using frozen HEOR FAME v3.1 (R7C) and fixed prompts; answer keys remained sealed. Outcomes included single-audit sensitivity, per-defect detection frequency, prespecified-decoy specificity, and exploratory two-audit union defect sensitivity.

Results. Sensitivity was 100.0% in 9 of 10 audits; one Markov audit detected 22/26 defects (84.6%). Descriptive pooled sensitivity was 96.9% for Markov (126/130 audit-defect opportunities) and 100.0% for PSM (140/140). Seven defects that individually changed the base-case conclusion were detected in every applicable audit (35/35 audit-defect opportunities); prespecified-decoy specificity was 100.0% (85/85 opportunities). All 20 retrospective within-model run-pair unions detected every defect.

Conclusions. In two development benchmarks, HEOR FAME detected nearly all seeded defects without flagging any decoys. detail.abstract: The amount by which earnings beat or miss the analyst consensus is reported in cents per share. We ask whether the market anchors on that nominal surprise in the sense of Tversky and Kahneman (1974), starting from the figure investors are shown and adjusting for expected earnings only in part, and find that it does. Using quarterly earnings announcements from 1990 to 2024, we show that three-day abnormal returns rise with the nominal surprise, holding the percentage surprise fixed. The nominal surprise equals the percentage surprise times expected earnings per share, the earnings base, so the same percentage surprise represents a larger nominal surprise when the base is larger. Consistent with anchoring, the response to a given percentage surprise more than doubles from the lowest to the eighth decile of the base. Holding total expected earnings fixed, the response falls as the share count rises, including through stock splits, which change the nominal surprise without changing the firm. The pattern is not explained by firm-specific response slopes, analyst measurement error, earnings yields, persistence, smoothing, greater information about future earnings, or established scale effects, implying that investors anchor on the cents in which earnings news is reported.

detail.abstract: Existing literature relying on administrative register data finds a residual gender wage gap of 6-8 percent after accounting for working time and sorting across jobs and employers. These studies, however, do not observe workers' skills. We examine whether direct measures of skills and skill use can reduce this residual. We link the Norwegian sample of the second cycle of the OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) to administrative payroll and job records for 2,700 workers aged 25-65. This places assessed numeracy and reported skill use in the same wage equation as contracted hours and job allocation. After working time and sorting are accounted for, women earn about 7 percent less than men, consistent with previous studies. Direct skill measures reduce this gap to about 5 percent, accounting for roughly one third of the residual, independently of the order in which the variables enter. Women have more formal education than men but lower measured numeracy and less frequent skill use, so controlling for education alone leaves these differences in the residual. Skill use contributes more than numeracy and likely captures sorting into different tasks within broad occupation-industry cells. Gender-by-skill interactions show no evidence of different returns to the same skills. A gap of about 5 percent nevertheless remains among workers with the same measured skills, skill use, hours and placement, and it persists across the middle of the distribution. Direct skill measures thus bring us closer to what drives the part of the gender wage gap that register data leave unexplained.
